Both changes are in. Diff is 61/61 — no line-count change, no hard wraps introduced, no other file touched.

Removed all ~90 commit-SHA citations across §1–§6, including the intro promise that each rule "cites the commit(s) that taught it"; narrative passages (walking skeleton, cadence, revert-and-narrate, lapse anatomy, meta-artifact lapses, restoration branch) keep their lessons with hashes replaced by role descriptions ("the skeleton commit", "the retrofit", "one such commit"), and PR #18 / file:line references are kept.
Renamed the §3 heading "The high-water mark: `1d1fb34`" to "the filter-delegation spec"; the quoted RED code block is unchanged.
Rewrote the fa0bc72 story in three places to the mock-lookup mechanics: §2.7 "The patch target is part of the specification" now explains that `mock.patch` binds where a name is looked up, that the library-targeted RED could not run against a from-importing CLI, and that re-pointing it was mechanical — keeping "when a GREEN commit edits a RED test, that edit is the thing to review".
§4(a) retitled "The patch target was corrected; the contract behind it was never written", labeled *not a violation; an unspecified requirement*, with the concrete reason the original RED could never have passed and the import style affirmed as canonical.
§3's high-water-mark closer no longer says the lapse "destroyed" it; it notes the mechanical correction and that the technique survives intact.
§5 item 1 reframed from "delegation property still unspecified / fa0bc72's inversion is live" to "The borrow has never been specified", with the repair reduced to `assert cli.SUPPORTED_FILTERS is library.SUPPORTED_FILTERS` and an explicit "the import style stays as it is"; item 6's cross-reference updated to "once #1 is settled".
